results.name: Seated Single Leg Hamstring Stretch
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight in front of you.
Bend your left knee and place the sole of your left foot against your right inner thigh. Keep your right leg extended and straight.
Reach forward with both hands towards your right foot, keeping your back straight. Aim to grasp your toes or reach as far as comfortable.

Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, feeling the stretch in your right hamstring. Slowly release and return to the starting position. Repeat on the other side by extending your left leg and bending your right knee.
tips: Keep your extended leg straight and avoid locking your knee to protect the joint.
Ensure your bent knee is relaxed and the sole of your foot is comfortably placed against your inner thigh.
Move into the stretch gradually and with control to prevent muscle strain or injury.
results.description: Seated Single Leg Hamstring Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Calves.

results.name: Seated Single Leg Toe Touch Hamstring Stretch
instructions: Sit with one leg extended and the other bent, foot against the inner thigh.
Sit tall and face the extended leg.
Hinge forward from your hips and reach toward your toes.
Hold, then switch sides.
tips: Keep your back long.
Don't bounce.
results.description: Seated Single Leg Toe Touch Hamstring Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Lower Back.

results.name: Seated Straight Leg Calf Stretch
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight in front of you.
Lightly bend both knees and extend your right foot, reaching forward to grasp your toes with your right hand.
Gently pull your toes towards you, feeling the stretch in your calf muscle.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then slowly release. Repeat on the left leg.
tips: Maintain a straight back as you reach forward to enhance the effectiveness of the stretch.
Engage your core muscles to support your lower back and avoid rounding your shoulders.
Move slowly and with control to prevent overstretching or injury.
results.description: Seated Straight Leg Calf Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings.

results.name: Seated Toe Touch Hamstrings Stretch
instructions: Sit with both legs extended in front of you.
Sit tall and reach your arms forward.
Hinge from your hips and reach toward your toes.
Hold, breathing slowly.
tips: Bend your knees slightly if needed.
Relax your neck.
results.description: Seated Toe Touch Hamstrings Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Lower Back.

results.name: Seated Twist
instructions: Sit tall with your legs extended.
Bend one knee and place that foot outside the opposite knee.
Twist toward the bent knee, using your opposite arm against the knee to deepen the twist.
Hold, then switch sides.
tips: Lengthen your spine on each inhale.
Twist a little further on each exhale.
results.description: Seated Twist is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Glutes.

results.name: Side Bend Standing Lats Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart.
Reach one arm overhead.
Lean to the opposite side until you feel a stretch along your side.
Hold, then switch sides.
tips: Keep your hips centred.
Don't lean forward or back.
results.description: Side Bend Standing Lats Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

results.name: Side Chest Stretch on Wall
instructions: Stand beside a wall and place your forearm and palm against it at shoulder height.
Step forward with the leg nearest the wall.
Gently turn your body away from the wall until you feel a stretch across your chest.
Hold, then switch sides.
tips: Change the height of your arm to stretch different parts of the chest.
Don't force the stretch.
results.description: Side Chest Stretch on Wall is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Front Shoulders, Biceps.

results.name: Side Lying Floor Stretch
instructions: Lie on your left side with your legs stacked on top of each other and your body in a straight line. Rest your head on your left arm.
Extend your right arm straight over your head.
Slowly lower your right hand towards your left hand to stretch your back.

Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, feeling the stretch in your back and shoulders. Slowly return to the starting position and repeat on the other side by lying on your right side and following the same steps.
tips: Ensure your extended arm stays straight to maximize the stretch in your back and shoulders.
Keep your core engaged to support your lower back during the stretch.
Perform the stretch on a comfortable, non-slip surface to ensure safety and reduce discomfort.
results.description: Side Lying Floor Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

results.name: Side Wrist Pull Stretch
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Extend your right arm across your torso at chest height, keeping it bent and your forearm parallel to the floor.
Bend your left arm and use your left hand to grasp your right hand, gently pulling your right wrist backward to feel a stretch in your right wrist and forearm.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then slowly release. Repeat on the other side.
tips: Move your wrist slowly and with control to avoid any sudden movements that could cause strain.
Breathe deeply and steadily as you hold the stretch.
Focus on relaxing into the stretch to allow your muscles to lengthen fully.
results.description: Side Wrist Pull Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Single Arm Extended Pull Downwards Biceps Stretch
instructions: Extend one arm in front of you, palm facing up.
With your other hand, gently pull your fingers down toward the floor.
Keep your arm straight until you feel a stretch in your biceps and forearm.
Hold, then switch arms.
tips: Keep your elbow straight.
Pull gently.
results.description: Single Arm Extended Pull Downwards Biceps Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.
